title: Tilde commutes with the unbounded total tensor complex
statement: For a commutative ring A and arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes P and N of A-modules, localization Q [def-pc-derived-category] of the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] of their termwise tilde sheaves on Spec(A) is naturally isomorphic, in both factors, to Q of the termwise tilde of the total module tensor complex. No K-flatness is required. Tilde is the associated-sheaf functor [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections].

source.place: Tag 08DX, lemma-quasi-coherence-tensor-product, proof of (2); termwise tensor comparison Tag 01I8

proof.text: Choose the affine tensor comparison of Tag 01I8. This is a determined object, not an arbitrary witness: its global linear map is prescribed on pure tensors, which generate, and the sheaf extension is uniquely prescribed by the tilde-global-sections adjunction. The theorem gives that this sheaf morphism is invertible.

To prove naturality in each module, use injectivity of the hom-equivalence of the tilde-global-sections adjunction and extensionality on pure tensors. Naturality of tilde.toOpen and of tensor products of global sections identifies the two sides. Package the resulting invertible comparison as a natural isomorphism of bifunctors.

The tilde adjunction makes tilde a left adjoint, hence it preserves the coproducts defining the unbounded total complex. It is additive, by preservation of binary coproducts in preadditive categories. Apply the already-proved natural total-bifunctor comparison in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.Bifunctor to the degreewise tensor natural isomorphism. This comparison respects both signed differentials and is invertible in every total degree. The complexes are those of def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves.

Apply DerivedCategory.Q to the inverse of every component of the total-complex natural isomorphism. Build the two-variable localized natural isomorphism using NatIso.ofComponents twice. Applying Q.map to the two naturality squares and using preservation of composition proves both naturality obligations.
